sentences.text: It buys you two days.
Then, on the twelfth night, a rope drops from the roof of the building next door.
Three people slide down it in white protective suits.
They carry a clipboard, a thermometer, and a very simple plan.
They know about the freezer.
They have been tracking it for days.
Problem four: the living.
You cannot fight three people with suits and tools.
But you understand something they do not.
If they cut the shutter, 250 dead walk in behind them.
And then nobody has a supermarket.
So you do not open the door.
You open the store.
One rope, one bucket, lowered off the back of the roof at 1:30 in the morning.
The first fifteen tins are free.
After that, you trade: batteries, fuel, medicine, news.
You worked retail for five years.
You know how to handle difficult customers.
House rule one, amended: nobody comes in, but the roof is open.
By day sixteen, there is a queue.
A woman with a baby, two old men with a wheelbarrow, and a girl on a bike who only ever asks for cat food.
On the seventeenth night, you finally catch the thing that has been moving your tins.
It is a small girl, nine years old, living in the ceiling.
Her name is Mina.
She has been up there since before the lights went out.
In her backpack, one enormous orange cat.
On day twenty, the bucket comes up with a note in it.
The people in white suits are done trading.
They are coming tonight.
They do not want the food.
They want whatever is behind the door that says do not open.
